questions.question:
D1 — Review focus for the dashboard plan
Project/branch/task: main, design review of the User Dashboard Page plan (review-input.md).
ELI10: I've rated this plan 4/10 on design completeness. The data and safety rules are solid, but it never says what the user sees first, how the three panels sit on phone vs desktop, or what the empty/error/toast/modal moments actually say and do. I'll generate visual mockups next, then review all 7 design dimensions. You can narrow that to specific areas instead.
Stakes if we pick wrong: Narrowing too early leaves gaps like toast accessibility or mobile layout for the implementer to guess at, and they ship as generic defaults.
Recommendation: A because the gaps span hierarchy, states, responsive and a11y, so a partial pass would miss real issues.
Completeness: A=10/10, B=6/10
Pros / cons:
A) Full review, all 7 passes (recommended)
  ✅ Covers hierarchy, states, journey, slop risk, design system, responsive and a11y
  ✅ Every gap gets its own decision so nothing is silently assumed
  ❌ More questions to answer, one per real gap found across the passes
B) Focus on specific areas only
  ✅ Fewer questions if you only care about, say, states and mobile layout
  ✅ Faster path to an amended plan for the areas you name
  ❌ Unreviewed dimensions stay at their current low rating and ship as guesses
Net: Full coverage with more decisions, versus speed with known blind spots.

options.label: Full review, all 7 (recommended)
options.description: Mockups, then all 7 passes. ✅ Covers every dimension. ✅ Each gap decided individually. ❌ More questions overall.

options.label: Focus on specific areas
options.description: Name the areas in a note. ✅ Fewer questions. ✅ Faster. ❌ Other dimensions remain unreviewed guesses.

questions.question:
Want outside design voices before the detailed review?
D2 — Outside design voices
Project/branch/task: main, design review of the User Dashboard Page plan.
ELI10: Optionally, two other reviewers read the plan before my 7 passes: Codex checks hard design rules and a litmus scorecard, and an independent Claude subagent checks completeness. Their disagreements get raised in the relevant pass.
Stakes if we pick wrong: Skipping means one reviewer's eye; running costs a few minutes and may only get one voice if Codex is missing.
Recommendation: No, proceed without — this is a taste call, no strong preference either way
Note: options differ in kind, not coverage — no completeness score.
Pros / cons: see option descriptions.
Net: A cross-model check versus the shortest path to a fixed plan.

options.label: Yes, run outside design voices
options.description: ✅ Codex hard-rule + litmus scorecard plus an independent Claude completeness read. ✅ Disagreements surface with both perspectives in the relevant pass. ❌ Adds a few minutes; Codex may be missing here, in which case only the Claude voice runs and it's tagged single-model.

options.label: No, proceed without (recommended)
options.description: ✅ Straight into the 7 passes with the approved mockup as anchor. ✅ Fewest steps to a fixed plan. ❌ Findings rest on one reviewer; no cross-model check on slop risk or hierarchy.

questions.question:
D3 — 1: What does a just-logged-in user see first, second, third?
Project/branch/task: main, User Dashboard plan, Pass 1 Information Architecture.
ELI10: The plan has three panels but no order. If we don't pick, the engineer puts them in a grid of three equal boxes and nobody knows where to look. Only notifications ask the user to do something, so they're the natural anchor.
Stakes if we pick wrong: Users skim past the one thing needing attention, or the page feels like a generic widget grid.
Recommendation: 1A because unread notifications are the only actionable content, and Krug says each screen needs one obvious next step.
Note: options differ in kind, not coverage — no completeness score.
Pros / cons:
A) Action row, then Notifications primary, Activity secondary (recommended)
  ✅ The one actionable thing (unread items) gets the wide main column and first scan
  ✅ Quick actions sit in the page header as a compact row, one primary button
  ❌ Activity feed is visually demoted; heavy activity users scroll or look right
B) Activity primary, Notifications in a side rail
  ✅ Suits products where 'what changed' matters more than inbox triage
  ✅ Notifications rail stays visible while scanning activity history
  ❌ Unread items compete in a narrow rail and are easier to ignore
Net: Anchor on what needs action (notifications) or on what changed (activity).

options.label: 1A Notifications primary (recommended)
options.description: Header + quick-action row first, Notifications wide main column second, Activity secondary column third.
